chunks: And among what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If you catch the Imam while he has already gone into rukuʿ, and you pronounce takbir and perform rukuʿ before he raises his head, then you have caught the rakʿah. But if the Imam raises his head before you go into rukuʿ, then it has passed you by.

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we understand his saying, 'if you catch him while he is in rukuʿ,' and in the last report, 'while he has already bowed,' as referring to joining him in the row, from which one should not remain behind when able, even if he had already caught the takbir of rukuʿ before that place.

Because whoever hears the Imam pronouncing takbir for rukuʿ while there is a distance between them, it is permissible for him to pronounce takbir and bow with him wherever the place comes to an end for him; then he may walk while in his rukuʿ, if he wishes, until he catches up with him, or he may perform sajdah in his place.

Then when he finishes his two sajdahs, he joins him. Whichever of these he wishes, he may do. And whenever we understand these two reports in this manner, the reports do not contradict one another. And that which indicates the permissibility of what we have mentioned is:

key_terms.الصَّفِّ: the row of worshippers in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the prayer leader in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةَ الرُّكُوعِ: the utterance of takbir associated with entering rukuʿ
key_terms.رَكَعَ: entered into rukuʿ, the bowing posture of salat (prayer)
key_terms.رُكُوعِهِ: his state of rukuʿ, the bowing posture
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيْهِ: his two sajdahs, the two prostrations of the rakʿah

ai.seo_question: When does a person catch the rakʿah if joining the Imam during rukuʿ in congregational salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of catching a rakʿah in congregational salat (prayer), specifically when joining the Imam during rukuʿ. It explains that one catches the rakʿah if one enters rukuʿ before the Imam raises his head, and it also clarifies how apparently differing reports may be reconciled regarding joining the row and moving to reach the Imam.
